title: a-decided-gap-lands-in-the-line-it-settles
author: cc
watchme: none, because of Akien's 2026-09-30 ruling on probes: "all probes respond to events" and "if it's not consumed, it's trash". The watch as cast fired on the beat and named consumers (CC at session open, codemother) that no code reads the probe's output into. The before/after comparison it wanted is not lost: the standing baseline (77 tickets rehearsed, 71 reached clean, median 4 records to clean, mean 4.15, measured 2026-10-02) is written in the proof's docstring, so passes-to-clean after this build can be measured over CairnCommons/rehearsals/ whenever a consumer asks. Event-fired probes are ticket 164da559823d's.
intention: A gap disposed with `cairn rehearse --decide` settles the decision it names: the reader is handed that answer inside the settled decision's line, and every decision carries its own D<n> label in the text it is handed.
why: Akien, 2026-09-29, on the rehearsal's intention: "It's so we can tell if the ticket is detailed enough. that's all. and right now, we're not trying to learn from those specifically, but we will be later on. we want our graph trees to BECOME the rehersal pass eventually. and the best way to do that is our graph trees along side haiku." His 2026-09-23 answer (open-a57cdd7cf3c1) is built — prompt.md tells the reader to judge the whole list (commit 3a6f0691). Measured 2026-09-29 on cd8096f9eeca: two passes refused 'missing D16..D20' because decide lines carry no D<n> in their text, and a settled line was re-flagged while its answer stood as a separate unlabeled line. Every wasted pass is time and money spent re-deriving a settled answer (Law 1), and the records these passes leave are what the graph trees will learn the reader from.
traces_to: Law 1 (a settled answer the reader cannot see is re-derived every pass); Akien's review bandwidth (a cap that fires on a settled ticket lands at his gate).
how: render() hands the reader a decisions view in which every decision's text starts with its D<n> and every rehearsal-sourced decision's text is also appended inside the line its step names. The ticket bytes and their hash are unchanged; only the rendered view changes.

falsifier.proves_green: GREEN when render() shows each decision as 'D<n> ...', a rehearsal-sourced decision's text appears inside the line of the decision its step names, the 'missing D<n>' refusal from decide lines cannot recur, and median passes-to-clean over the next 10 tickets rehearsed is at or below the standing median.
falsifier.wrong_intent: WRONG INTENT if readers keep re-flagging a step whose answer is rendered inside it — then the reader is the defect, not the render.
falsifier.proves_red: DONE when, over a scratch commons ticket (never the live corpus): (1) render() shows every decision's text beginning 'D<n> ' with its own n, including a decision whose stored text carries no label; (2) a decision with source 'rehearsal' and step 'D<m>' appears inside D<m>'s rendered text as '[settled by D<n>: <its text>]', and stays in the list labeled; (3) render() still returns the sha256 of the ticket file bytes; (4) the ticket file's bytes are unchanged by render(). RED before the build: the render pastes the file verbatim, so (1) and (2) fail.

links.what: Akien's 2026-09-23 answer: the reader judges the whole decision list — built in prompt.md 3a6f0691
where it was measured: two refusals and a re-flag

decisions.text: D1 WHAT render() DOES TODAY (rehearsal.py:205): pastes the ticket file verbatim inside a ```json block under '# THE TICKET', then the chart berths, then ref'd charters. The hash it returns is of the file bytes and stays so.

D2 THE VIEW: render() parses the ticket and, before pasting, rewrites ONLY the pasted copy's decisions list: (a) each entry whose text does not already start with 'D<n>' (its own n) gets 'D<n> ' prefixed; (b) for each entry with source == 'rehearsal' and a step of the form 'D<m>' naming an entry in the list, the entry D<m>'s pasted text gains ' [settled by D<n>: <that entry's text>]'. The rehearsal entry itself stays in the list, labeled. A step that is not 'D<m>' or names no entry is left alone. The pasted copy is json.dumps(doc, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False).
D3 decide() (rehearsal.py:531) is unchanged: the file keeps who said what and when; the fold is a render-time view.

D4 THE BASELINE: before the build lands, measure passes-to-clean per ticket over CairnCommons/rehearsals/*.json as the NUMBER OF RECORDS for the ticket, in 'at' order, up to and including its first clean one. NOT the record's 'pass' field: it restarts after every --decide (measured 2026-10-02: its median over first-clean records is 1, while the record count's is 4). Measured 2026-10-02: 77 tickets rehearsed, 71 reached clean, median 4 records to clean, mean 4.15. Write the median, the population and the date into the proof's docstring as the standing baseline.

D5 THE PROOF: cairn/machines/rehearsal/proofs/test_decide_lands_in_its_line.py, prove-first: a scratch commons ticket with decisions D1 (no label in text), D2, and a rehearsal entry D3 with step 'D1'; teeth — (1) rendered text contains 'D1 ' at the start of D1's text; (2) D1's rendered line contains '[settled by D3: ' and D3's text; (3) the returned sha equals sha256 of the file bytes; (4) the file bytes are unchanged after render. Every output marked testing.

The population is both numbers, named: 77 tickets rehearsed, of which 71 reached clean; the median (4) and mean (4.15) are over the 71. The proof docstring states it so (already written at cairn/machines/rehearsal/proofs/test_decide_lands_in_its_line.py).

The proof is a plain python script (exit 0 = green), already written and committed red at cairn/machines/rehearsal/proofs/test_decide_lands_in_its_line.py. The testing mark: its fixture ticket id and title carry 'testing-eb1c943e09b9', and its scratch commons comes from cairn.tools.scratch.scratch.scratch_dir('testing-eb1c943e09b9-decide-lands-') and is removed with shutil.rmtree when the run ends. Nothing is written to the live commons.
